findings.statement: Prospective review is mandatory: the State plan must provide for a review of drug therapy before each prescription is filled or delivered to a beneficiary, and the State must give pharmacies detailed information on how to comply (counseling, profiling, documentation), which pharmacies must pass on to their pharmacists [42-CFR-456.705(a)].

The review is specifically point-of-sale or point-of-distribution review of drug therapy using predetermined standards before each prescription is filled or delivered, and it 'must include screening to identify potential drug therapy problems' [42-CFR-456.705(b)].

The required screening problem types are: (1) therapeutic duplication — two or more drugs from the same therapeutic class whose combined daily dose risks an adverse result or adds program cost without added benefit; (2) drug-disease contraindication; (3) adverse drug-drug interaction; (4) incorrect drug dosage (dosage = strength × quantity dispensed ÷ day's supply, outside the predetermined standard); (5) incorrect duration of treatment; (6) drug-allergy interactions; (7) clinical abuse/misuse [42-CFR-456.705(b), 42-CFR-456.705(b)-2].
